name: Appleman and Complicated Task
description: Toastman came up with a very complicated task. He gives it to Appleman, but Appleman doesn't know how to solve it. Can you help him? Given a n × n checkerboard. Each cell of the board has either character ' x ', or character ' o ', or nothing. How many ways to fill all the empty cells with ' x ' or ' o ' (each cell must contain only one character in the end) are there, such that for each cell the number of adjacent cells with ' o ' will be even? Find the number of ways modulo 1000000007 (10 9 + 7) . Two cells of the board are adjacent if they share a side.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers n , k ( 1 ≤ n , k ≤ 10 5 ) — the size of the board, and the number of cells that has characters initially. Then k lines follows. The i -th line contains two integers and a character: a i , b i , c i ( 1 ≤ a i , b i ≤ n ; c i is either ' o ' or ' x '). This line means: there is a character c i in the cell that is located on the intersection of the a i -th row and b i -th column. All the given cells are distinct. Consider that the rows are numbered from 1 to n from top to bottom. Analogically, the columns are numbered from 1 to n from left to right.
output_specification: Print a single integer — the answer to the problem.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 461D — Appleman and Complicated Task [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
